> Dear Greg,
>
> I ran into this last night; suspect this is a bug with the 'invert' option. Below is the code with the nat example neuron to reproduce the bug. If I set invert option as FALSE, it works.
>
> -------------------------------------------------
> library(igraph)
> library(nat)
> n1 = Cell07PNs[[1]]
> idx = 48 # just pick an idx of any node in the neuron
> n_graph_dfs = igraph::dfs(as.ngraph(n1), root = idx, "out", unreachable = FALSE)
> n1_subset=subset(n1, n_graph_dfs$order, invert = T)
> -------------------------------------------------
>
> The above code return:
>
> Error in as.igraph.vs(graph, v) :
> Cannot use a vertex sequence from another graph.
>
>
> Best regards,
>
> Zhihao

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: bug with the 'invert' option in subset function (nat)?
parts:
On 23 Jan 2016, at 15:17, Zheng, Zhihao wrote:

> library(igraph)
> library(nat)
> n1 = Cell07PNs[[1]]
> idx = 48 # just pick an idx of any node in the neuron
> n_graph_dfs = igraph::dfs(as.ngraph(n1), root = idx, "out",
> unreachable = FALSE)
> n1_subset=subset(n1, n_graph_dfs$order, invert = T)

Hmm, so it turns out that this works:

n1_subset=subset(n1, na.omit(as.integer(n_graph_dfs$order)), invert = T)

The reason is that n_graph_dfs$order is not an integer vector but a
special class "igraph.vs" which is attached to a specific graph. The
igraph library then checks that you are trying to use the vertex
sequence with that graph and not another graph for which it may not be
relevant. In this case that check fails although the vertex sequence is
in fact perfectly well aligned with the neuron.

It's not exactly my bug, but I will defend against it in future (you'll
get notified when the github issue is closed).

na.omit is required because subset.neuron and the underlying
prune_vertices expect real index ids – again I can remove the NAs for
user protection.

Best,

Greg.

>> library(igraph)
>> library(nat)
>> n1 = Cell07PNs[[1]]
>> idx = 48 # just pick an idx of any node in the neuron
>> n_graph_dfs = igraph::dfs(as.ngraph(n1), root = idx, "out",
>> unreachable = FALSE)
>> n1_subset=subset(n1, n_graph_dfs$order, invert = T)

So this is fixed now, details at
https://github.com/jefferis/nat/issues/288. Incidentally you may be
interested in the spine function. This can return either what we call
the spine of a neuron (the longest path, optionally starting from the
root) ar the inverse of that.
